title: A Theory of Information Architecture for Networked Decisions: Freshness, Locality, and Coordination
summary: Networked systems face a tradeoff between the scope of the information behind a decision and its freshness: a broader view of the system supports better coordination, but assembling and communicating it takes time, so it arrives older. We study this tradeoff for a team of agents that repeatedly choose actions to minimize a shared quadratic cost driven by an environment that evolves on its own, unaffected by the agents' actions.
